# Introduction

## About this template

This is a **Typst-based report template** for the University of Hamburg. It produces a PDF with cover page, title page, table of contents, running headers, and page numbers -- all without requiring a LaTeX/TeX installation.

Configure the YAML header including the following elements:

- `title`, `subtitle`: Document title and subtitle
- `author`: List of authors with name, affiliation numbers, and email
- `affiliations`: List of affiliations with number, name, department, address
- `date`: Date of the document
- `logo1`, `logo2`: Logos for the left and right side of the title page
- `abstract`: Shown on the title page (remove to skip)
- `cover-bg-image`: Background image for the cover page (remove to skip cover)
- `cover-page-color`, `cover-text-color`: Colors for the cover page
- `cover-fade-effect`: Gradient overlay on cover image
- `mainfont`: Choose between "Helvetica Neue" (default) and "TheSansUHH"

The font is set when running the function, e.g., `UHHformats::create_quarto_doc(dirname = "my_report", template = "typst_report", font = "TheSansUHH")`.


## Advantages of Typst over LaTeX

- **No TeX installation required** -- Typst is bundled with Quarto (version 1.4+)
- **Much faster compilation** -- milliseconds instead of seconds
- **Simpler template syntax** -- easier to customize
- Cover page with gradient fade effect, title page with author affiliations, and styled TOC


## Cross-references

Cross-references work as in other Quarto formats: `@fig-label` for figures, `@tbl-label` for tables, `@sec-label` for sections.

See @tbl-kable in @sec-tables and @fig-base in @sec-figures.

# Results

## R output

```{r}
mtcars <- read.csv("data/mtcars.csv")
summary(mtcars[,1:4])
```


## Tables {#sec-tables}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-kable
#| tbl-cap: "This is a table produced with knitr::kable()."
df <- mtcars[1:5, 1:6]
knitr::kable(df)
```


## Figures {#sec-figures}

```{r}
#| label: fig-base
#| fig-cap: "Relationship between horsepower and fuel economy."
plot(mtcars$hp, mtcars$mpg,
xlab = "Gross Horsepower",
ylab = "Miles Per Gallon",
pch = 19)
abline(lm(mpg ~ hp, data = mtcars), col = "red")
```
